questions.prompt: Which of these is a non-functional requirement?

options.text: A user can shorten a long URL
The redirect must complete in under 100 milliseconds
A user can delete their account
The system emails a receipt after purchase

questions.explanation: A latency target describes how well the system must perform, not what feature it provides, so it is a non-functional requirement. The others are features (functional requirements).

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a fault and a failure?

options.text: A fault is a user error; a failure is a bug
A fault is one component misbehaving; a failure is the whole system not delivering its service
A fault happens in testing; a failure happens in production

questions.explanation: A fault is a single component going wrong. A failure is the system as a whole failing to do its job. Fault-tolerant design keeps faults from becoming failures.

questions.prompt: Which three properties does Designing Data-Intensive Applications use to frame good systems? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: DDIA frames system design around reliability, scalability, and maintainability. Profitability is a business concern, not one of these three.

questions.prompt: The single component that limits the whole system's performance is called the ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: The bottleneck is the limiting component; improving anything else won't help until you address it.

questions.prompt: A team with zero users builds sharded databases and a dozen microservices 'to be scalable.' What is the main problem?

options.text: Nothing — you can never be too scalable
They traded away simplicity, maintainability, and cost to solve a problem they don't have yet

questions.explanation: Scalability trades against simplicity, maintainability, and cost. Designing for load you don't have buys complexity you must pay for now.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: How long a single request takes
How many requests are handled per unit of time
Keeping working correctly when faults occur
How easily people can operate and change the system

questions.explanation: Latency is per-request time; throughput is volume over time; reliability is correctness under faults; maintainability is the human cost of running and evolving the system.
